_doc: Every effect, what perceptual resource it claims, and what it costs. Two effects compose badly when they claim the same resource, because a reader has one of each and cannot spend it twice. That is the whole model: conflict is resource contention, not a taste opinion, which is why it can be checked.

_resources.FOCUS: Where the eye goes first. There is exactly one. Two things claiming it means neither has it.
_resources.DEPTH: The cue that says what is in front. Parallax, scale, blur, shadow and overlap all encode it, and mixing two encodings reads as a mistake rather than as depth.
_resources.READING: Attention held on text. Anything moving in the same viewport spends it.
_resources.SCROLL: One input, shared by everything scroll-linked. Past a few claimants the mapping becomes unreadable.
_resources.TIME: The arrival sequence. Two staggers running at once have no order.
_resources.SURFACE: The page's one bright or saturated area. A second one halves the first.
_resources.POINTER: Hover and cursor feedback. Two responses to one movement reads as jitter.

effects.note: Val Head lists it as a vestibular trigger. The variable is virtual distance covered, not duration.
Native position:sticky. Scroll stays one to one, nothing intercepts the wheel.
Playhead bound to scroll offset. Reads as magic and cannot be faked with keyframes.
Scroll drives state, the state decides what renders. Nothing animates, so an animation-only capture calls it static. Most underused effect there is.
Travel 16 to 32px. 400px is a ride. Once, never re-triggered.
A 3D zoom over large virtual distance is on the vestibular list.
Val Head's safe list: opacity, colour and blur are unlikely to be problematic.
stroke-dashoffset with pathLength=1. One animation per primitive, 600 to 800ms linear, 15 to 20ms stagger.
30 to 80ms per item, and (n-1)*step must stay under 400ms. Cap the count, not the delay.
Pauses on hover or it is unreadable by design.
linear only. An eased loop pulses. Defensible only where the motion IS the product.
Claims focus permanently, because the eye tracks its own cursor.
Gate behind (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine) or touch fires it on every tap.
transform only. Settles rather than snapping.
100 to 160ms, scale(0.97), ease-out. Press and release must not share a duration.
Never autoplay with sound. Competes with every word next to it.
Named as the AI-default signature. Linear and Resend both ban atmospheric gradients outright.
backdrop-filter. A second depth encoding on top of a surface ladder is one too many.
Four steps plus hairlines. The cheapest way to make a dark page read expensive.
Banned in dark interfaces by Linear, Resend, Raycast, Warp and Cursor independently.
One accent, at most four named places. Von Restorff: exactly one per section.
A control the reader can drive. Beats any amount of decoration for holding attention.
Must render its final value in static HTML or a crawler and a screen reader get the placeholder.
Lenis and friends. Disable entirely under reduced motion: hijacked scroll is the most disorienting thing for anyone with it set.

rules.when: more than one effect claims FOCUS in the same viewport
rules.why: There is one first place the eye goes. Two claimants means neither is it, and the reader picks at random.
rules.fix: Demote all but one. A second bright surface becomes a ghost, a second accent becomes neutral.

rules.when: more than two effects claim DEPTH
rules.why: Parallax, scale, blur, shadow and glass all say the same thing in different languages. Three at once reads as a mistake rather than as depth. Hobday: do not mix depth techniques.
rules.fix: Pick the surface ladder OR shadows OR parallax. Not two, never three.

rules.when: a CONSTANT effect shares a viewport with prose the reader is meant to finish
rules.why: Continuous motion pulls at peripheral vision the whole time the eye is on the text. Defensible only where the motion IS the product being sold.
rules.fix: Move the loop out of the reading viewport, or stop it while that section is in view.

rules.when: more than three effects are SCROLL-LINKED at the same scroll position
rules.why: They all read from one number. Past a few, the reader cannot tell which of their own movements caused what.
rules.fix: Sequence them across different scroll ranges instead of stacking them on one.

rules.when: two or more SCROLL-LINKED effects share a range at the same rate
rules.why: Identical rate is a sheet of paper sliding. Different rates against the same scroll is what produces depth.
rules.fix: Give them different multipliers, or drop one to STATIC.

rules.why: Stagger communicates arrival order. Two at once have no order, so it reads as noise arriving.
rules.fix: Sequence them, or collapse both into one stagger across the union.

rules.when: more than one vestibular-flagged effect is active at a scroll position
rules.why: Val Head's trigger list is cumulative. Parallax plus scroll-scrub plus smooth scroll is three at once.
rules.fix: One at most, and every one gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.

rules.when: more than one effect claims POINTER on the same element
rules.why: One movement producing two responses reads as jitter, not as responsiveness.
rules.fix: Keep the one closest to the thing being pointed at.

rules.when: fewer than 60 percent of substantial elements are STATIC
rules.why: Motion means something only against stillness. A page where most things move has no emphasis left to spend.
rules.fix: Demote everything that is moving for decoration rather than for meaning.
